Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Internationalism. Ultimately from Ancient Greek ἐμπάθεια (empátheia) through 20th century English empathy.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈempɑtiɑ/, [ˈe̞mpɑ̝ˌt̪iɑ̝]
  • Rhymes: -iɑ
  • Syllabification(key): em‧pa‧ti‧a
  • Hyphenation(key): em‧pa‧tia

Noun

[edit]

empatia

  1. empathy

Polish

[edit]
Polish Wikipedia has an article on:
empatia
Wikipedia pl

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from English empathy, from Ancient Greek ἐμπάθεια (empátheia).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ɛmˈpa.tja/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -atja
  • Syllabification: em‧pa‧tia

Noun

[edit]

empatia f

  1. (psychology) empathy (intellectual identification with another person)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of empatia
singular
nominative empatia
genitive empatii
dative empatii
accusative empatię
instrumental empatią
locative empatii
vocative empatio

Derived terms

[edit]
adjective
  • empatyczny

[edit]

  • empatia in Polish dictionaries at PWN

Portuguese

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): (careful pronunciation) /ẽ.paˈt͡ʃi.ɐ/, (natural pronunciation) /ĩ.paˈt͡ʃi.ɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): (careful pronunciation) /ẽ.paˈt͡ʃi.ɐ/, (natural pronunciation) /ĩ.paˈt͡ʃi.ɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): (careful pronunciation) /ẽ.paˈt͡ʃi.a/, (natural pronunciation) /ĩ.paˈt͡ʃi.a/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ẽ.pɐˈti.ɐ/

  • Hyphenation: em‧pa‧ti‧a

Noun

[edit]

empatia f (plural empatias)

  1. empathy (capacity to understand another person’s point of view or feelings)
